about.heading: Hello, I'm Disu Ibukunoluwa.

projects.title: AML detection for cryptocurrency transactions
projects.category: Final-year project / Machine learning / Graph analytics
projects.summary: Built a graph-aware system to flag potentially illicit blockchain transactions using the Elliptic++ dataset. Combined GAT embeddings with a stacked Random Forest, XGBoost and Logistic Regression model; achieved 96.65% validation recall and 0.9315 ROC-AUC.
projects.challenge: Detect potentially illicit cryptocurrency transactions from blockchain activity, using both transaction-level features and the relationships between transactions. Deploy the resulting system despite the limited resources of a free hosting tier.
approach: Used the Elliptic++ dataset, which represents cryptocurrency transactions and their relationships as a graph.
Generated Graph Attention Network (GAT) embeddings to capture graph context alongside transaction features.
Trained a stacking ensemble: Random Forest and XGBoost predictions feed a Logistic Regression meta-learner. Training ran on Google Colab using a T4 GPU.
Deployed a working system to Render's free tier and cached embeddings to reduce resource demands.
projects.architecture: Elliptic++ transaction graph → GAT embeddings + transaction features → Random Forest and XGBoost → Logistic Regression meta-learner → illicit-transaction risk classification. Training: Google Colab (T4 GPU). Deployment: Render with embedding caching.

decisions.title: Add graph context
decisions.body: Use GAT embeddings to represent transaction relationships, rather than relying on isolated transaction features alone.

decisions.title: Combine complementary models
decisions.body: Use Random Forest and XGBoost as base learners, with Logistic Regression combining their outputs in a stacking ensemble.

decisions.title: Make deployment practical
decisions.body: Cache computed embeddings so the deployed system can operate within Render free-tier resource constraints.

projects.quality: The reported 96.65% recall and 0.9315 ROC-AUC are validation metrics, not a guarantee of performance on new or live blockchain transactions.
projects.outcomes: Approximately 96.65% validation recall for illicit transactions and a ROC-AUC of 0.9315. Delivered a working deployed system on Render rather than only a training notebook, using embedding caching to address free-tier constraints.
projects.lessons: Graph structure can provide useful context for transaction classification, while deployment constraints require practical choices such as caching expensive intermediate representations.

projects.title: Bitcoin price ETL pipeline
projects.summary: A scheduled ETL pipeline that collects Bitcoin quotes from the CoinMarketCap API, cleans and transforms them using Pandas, and loads them into PostgreSQL—with a timestamped CSV fallback if the database write fails.
projects.challenge: Collect, process and store Bitcoin market data on a consistent monthly schedule for historical market analysis and reporting.
approach: Extract Bitcoin quotes in USD from the CoinMarketCap API using an authenticated request.
Normalise and clean the returned JSON using Pandas, including numeric and datetime conversion.
Load structured records into PostgreSQL, writing the processed data to a timestamped CSV when the database load fails.
Orchestrate extract_data_task, transform_data_task and load_data_task in Apache Airflow and deploy using GitHub Actions.
projects.architecture: CoinMarketCap API → Airflow extraction → Pandas transformation → PostgreSQL (fallback: timestamped CSV). DAG: crypto_dag. Cron schedule: 0 0 1 * * (first day of each month). Configured start date: June 21, 2024.

decisions.title: Separate the ETL stages
decisions.body: Explicit extraction, transformation and loading tasks keep the stages easier to reason about.

decisions.title: Preserve data during database errors
decisions.body: A CSV fallback retains the transformed output rather than discarding it after a failed PostgreSQL write.

decisions.title: Automate deployment
decisions.body: GitHub Actions deploys the Airflow workflow to an Ubuntu server.

projects.quality: A timestamped CSV fallback protects transformed records when loading to PostgreSQL fails; it does not automatically retry database ingestion.
projects.outcomes: A monthly Bitcoin market data pipeline with scheduled ingestion, PostgreSQL storage, CSV fallback, and a GitHub Actions deployment workflow.
projects.lessons: Orchestration, consistent transformation and explicit handling of downstream failures are all part of reliable data engineering.
